doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

chapter: Back to Chicago and the road to jail and illness
title: Sonny Rollins at the Village Vanguard
summary: Rollins hires Ware and Elvin Jones for one track and records the whole live album; Ware turns down a tour to stay at Riverside.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Maybe you could talk; before you get in to that too much, maybe you can talk about this Sonny Rollins date that was at the Vanguard; that's an important date.
Oh yes. The night at the Village Vanguard.

Oh, well, one afternoon; no, the previous afternoon, I'm down at the Vanguard and Sonny had come up and he we had a bass player, Don Bailey, out of Baltimore, and La Roca Pete the drummer; they were working with Sonny, and Sonny said, "Hey Wilbur, I want you to come by tomorrow afternoon" -- now they had matinees down at the Vanguard at that time, and he said he was recording down there tomorrow and I want you to come by and do a track on my date."

And he said, "But I'll pay you for the whole date". It wasn't that much -- you know, a whole day I think. It was $50 or $75 or something like that. One side. And two sides, LP was a hundred and a quarter, I believe.

But anyway, I said, "Okay" and he said, "And you don't have to bring your bass" he said to Don, and Don said "Will it be all if he uses yours?" right for you here?" he and I said, "Yeah, that'd be fine."

So the next afternoon, I show up. Elvin Evelyn is sitting there, and so we're sitting there at the table, and Rudy Van Gelder's I look up there and they got all this equipment set up in Alfred Lion and Don and Pete are waiting on line, and Sonny. No, down in peak with Sonny and Sonny comes in and he doesn't say a word to us, he just walks back and goes on up toward the stage, so I'm thinking, I think, well, he's going up there and he'll want me to play a set, a warmup, and then call us to play whatever go into the tune he wants played.
So Pete sits down at the drums, and Don grabs his bass, and this is a live recording, and Sonny walks out to the

microphone. center stage, and says, "Will Elvin Evan Jones and Wilbur Ware come to the bandstand please?" and it was just like that. So, you know. Pete and Donald had to get up and they came back looking at us, odds but they knew we were gonna play, so it was just the idea that we would play first, so we get up there and Sonny turned to me and says, "I want to play Old Devil Moon" I said, "Wait a minute, Sonny; I'm not too sure of the changes on that one." and (unintelligible) and he laid some changes on me. I hadn't played the tune; I had heard it, but I hadn't played it to remember it well enough to record it, and he said, "Oh, you can hear it."

So I said, "Okay, let's take it" -- and we went from that in to something else; played the whole thing, the whole first side, and then he says, "Look," while they was changing the tapes, "I had to call these fellows up, you know, they were working with me and I want to let them play a tune", and I said, "Isn't that something?" He hired Elvin Evan and I just to play one track and here we wound up playing the whole gig date except for one track '.

But, you know, Elvin Evan and I thought, you know, since it wasn't rehearsed no emergency; it was spontaneous, a good feeling, thing, "Oh, this ain't nothing," but Sonny seemed to sense something; he felt real comfortable with what he was doing, because he asked us; he said, "Look man, I'm going on tour and I'm going out to the West Coast and from there I'm going to Paris, and I want you all to stay with me; I'll take care of

this, and anything you need, I'll get for you'. And I said, "No, man, I don't want to go." And that would have been my first chance to go to Europe. But heck, I was recording, you know, at Riverside and I didn't want to leave.
And when I made that album, they still say everybody heard thinks of that as a kind of a classic.
